topics.title: Equivalent fractions: Model and identify equivalent fractions as lengths on a number line

questions.stem: What fraction of this shape is shaded?
questions.hint: Count the TOTAL number of equal parts for the bottom number (denominator), and count how many parts are shaded for the top number (numerator).

keyPoints.text: fraction of this shape is shaded
keyPoints.note: Fraction = (shaded parts) / (total equal parts).

steps.explain: Count the total number of equal parts that make up the whole shape. Numbering every part shows there are \(6\) equal parts (denominator = \(6\)).

questions.hint: Count how many equal boxes make up the entire highlighted row — that count is the denominator of the unit fraction!

topics.title: Fractions greater than one: Represent fractional quantities equal to and greater than 1 whole

questions.stem: In the Fraction Maze, you count forward by quarters starting at \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) and ending at \(4\dfrac{3}{4}\). What are the next three numbers in the maze right after \(1\dfrac{3}{4}\)?
questions.hint: Add 1/4 each step: remember 1 3/4 + 1/4 = 1 4/4 = 2 whole!

keyPoints.note: Every 4 quarters makes the next whole number.

steps.explain: Add \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) to \(2\) to get \(2\dfrac{1}{4}\).
Add \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) again to get \(2\dfrac{2}{4}\).
Therefore, the next three numbers are \(2,\ 2\dfrac{1}{4},\ 2\dfrac{2}{4}\).

questions.stem: Write the improper fraction \(\dfrac{6}{4}\) as a whole number or mixed numeral.
questions.hint: Divide 6 by 4: the quotient is the whole number, and any remainder goes over 4.

keyPoints.note: Every 4 quarters (4/4) equals 1 whole.

steps.explain: Recall that \(\dfrac{4}{4} = 1\) whole. Divide the numerator \(6\) by \(4\).
The quotient \(1\) gives \(1\) whole (\(4\) quarters).
The remainder \(2\) becomes \(\dfrac{2}{4}\).
Therefore, \(\dfrac{6}{4} = 1\dfrac{2}{4}\).

questions.stem: Write the improper fraction \(\dfrac{12}{4}\) as a whole number or mixed numeral.
questions.hint: Divide 12 by 4: the quotient is the whole number, and any remainder goes over 4.

keyPoints.note: Every 4 quarters (4/4) equals 1 whole.

steps.explain: Recall that \(\dfrac{4}{4} = 1\) whole. Divide the numerator \(12\) by \(4\).
The quotient \(3\) gives \(3\) wholes (\(12\) quarters).
There is no remainder, so the result is an exact whole number.
Therefore, \(\dfrac{12}{4} = 3\).

questions.stem: Write the improper fraction \(\dfrac{11}{4}\) as a whole number or mixed numeral.
questions.hint: Divide 11 by 4: the quotient is the whole number, and any remainder goes over 4.

keyPoints.note: Every 4 quarters (4/4) equals 1 whole.

steps.explain: Recall that \(\dfrac{4}{4} = 1\) whole. Divide the numerator \(11\) by \(4\).
The quotient \(2\) gives \(2\) wholes (\(8\) quarters).
The remainder \(3\) becomes \(\dfrac{3}{4}\).
Therefore, \(\dfrac{11}{4} = 2\dfrac{3}{4}\).

questions.stem: Write the improper fraction \(\dfrac{9}{4}\) as a whole number or mixed numeral.
questions.hint: Divide 9 by 4: the quotient is the whole number, and any remainder goes over 4.

keyPoints.note: Every 4 quarters (4/4) equals 1 whole.

steps.explain: Recall that \(\dfrac{4}{4} = 1\) whole. Divide the numerator \(9\) by \(4\).
The quotient \(2\) gives \(2\) wholes (\(8\) quarters).
The remainder \(1\) becomes \(\dfrac{1}{4}\).
Therefore, \(\dfrac{9}{4} = 2\dfrac{1}{4}\).

questions.stem: Write the improper fraction \(\dfrac{7}{4}\) as a whole number or mixed numeral.
questions.hint: Divide 7 by 4: the quotient is the whole number, and any remainder goes over 4.

keyPoints.note: Every 4 quarters (4/4) equals 1 whole.

steps.explain: Recall that \(\dfrac{4}{4} = 1\) whole. Divide the numerator \(7\) by \(4\).
The quotient \(1\) gives \(1\) whole (\(4\) quarters).
The remainder \(3\) becomes \(\dfrac{3}{4}\).
Therefore, \(\dfrac{7}{4} = 1\dfrac{3}{4}\).

questions.stem: Write the improper fraction \(\dfrac{8}{4}\) as a whole number or mixed numeral.
questions.hint: Divide 8 by 4: the quotient is the whole number, and any remainder goes over 4.

keyPoints.note: Every 4 quarters (4/4) equals 1 whole.

steps.explain: Recall that \(\dfrac{4}{4} = 1\) whole. Divide the numerator \(8\) by \(4\).
The quotient \(2\) gives \(2\) wholes (\(8\) quarters).
There is no remainder, so the result is an exact whole number.
Therefore, \(\dfrac{8}{4} = 2\).

questions.stem: Write the improper fraction \(\dfrac{5}{4}\) as a mixed numeral.
questions.hint: Divide 5 by 4: 4 fits into 5 once with 1 quarter left over.

keyPoints.note: 4/4 = 1 whole, leaving 1/4.

steps.explain: Divide numerator 5 by denominator 4: \(5 \div 4 = 1\) remainder \(1\).
Write 4/4 as 1 whole.
Combine into a mixed numeral: \(1\dfrac{1}{4}\).
Therefore, \(\dfrac{5}{4} = 1\dfrac{1}{4}\).
